Yesterday, the US government announced an updated list of prohibited foreign-manufactured products, adding 'advanced robotic devices.' A spokesperson for the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) confirmed today that the ban also applies to robotic vacuum cleaners.

The robotic vacuum ban affects well-known brands like Roomba and Roborock, but you can continue to use your existing products

When the Trump administration announced yesterday a ban on 'advanced robotic devices' entering the United States, media attention focused on humanoid robots. Yet espionage doesn't require legs, and the FCC's robot ban is no exception. Katie Gorscak, the FCC's director of media relations, confirmed to The Verge that the ban also covers robotic vacuum cleaners. Your existing Roomba at home is not the target of the ban, and companies can continue to import and sell approved models. However, the government claims that future foreign robots will pose national security risks, and even robotic vacuum companies have suddenly been required to commit to manufacturing in the United States.

The FCC stated that advanced robotic devices carry national security risks, and the relevant regulations also apply to seemingly harmless products, such as robotic vacuum cleaners and robotic lawn mowers.

Unless a product is explicitly approved, or for example manufactured in the United States, it will not be allowed to be sold in the country.

The ban is expected to deal a particularly heavy blow to the robotic vacuum market, as top brands such as Roomba, Roborock, and Ecovacs are all owned by Chinese companies.

If you already own the relevant products, you can still use them today — the FCC won't come to your home to confiscate your robotic vacuum.

But depending on how the ban is enforced, the robotic vacuum market may undergo drastic changes in the short term. If this feels familiar, it's because this ban is very similar to the wireless router ban implemented a few months ago.

Will you continue to use your existing robotic vacuum? Why? Feel free to tell us in the comments section.
